guide_enrichment.narrative: We understand why Maryland’s start may attract attention. We saw the offense produce 475 yards at UConn, while Malik Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns. Maryland also avoided a turnover in each of its first two games. That is encouraging context, but we are not treating two clean performances as proof that the offense will sustain the same efficiency here.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, Nebraska’s rushing offense against Maryland’s run defense is the matchup that matters most. Maryland allowed only 38.5 rushing yards per game through its first two contests, but our rush EPA numbers still identify a meaningful advantage for Nebraska. The question is whether those early defensive results reflect a lasting strength or whether Nebraska can expose what our longer-run efficiency view considers the softer part of Maryland’s profile. With our overall expectation already closely aligned with the market, we do not see enough separation to move beyond a pass.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12, 2026.
Maryland produced 475 total yards, 27 first downs and no turnovers against UConn, with 350 passing yards and 125 rushing yards.
Maryland converted 8 of 15 third downs and possessed the ball for 35:31 against UConn.
Maryland held UConn to 223 total yards, including 67 rushing yards, and recorded five sacks.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Malik Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns against UConn, including a program-record 18 consecutive completions.
Through two games in 2026, Washington had completed 53 of 72 passes for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.
Washington started all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025 and passed for 2,963 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Transfer backup quarterback Cardell Williams completed 4 of 5 passes for 60 yards and a touchdown and rushed five times for 49 yards in the opener against Hampton.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's offensive line against UConn consisted of left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright; the unit blocked for 475 total yards.
Amory Hills made his first Maryland start at left guard against UConn after transfer Tellek Lockette started the opener there against Hampton.
Rahtrel Perry entered the guide with 39 consecutive career offensive-line starts, the most on Maryland's offense.

Transfer receivers Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. each exceeded 100 receiving yards at UConn: Gladding had eight catches for 130 yards and a touchdown, while Durr had 10 catches for 106 yards and a touchdown.
Harry Dalton III rushed for 48 yards and two touchdowns at UConn, while Iverson Howard rushed 14 times for 55 yards and a touchdown and caught three passes for nine yards.

Maryland added 17 offseason transfers, including receivers Gladding, Durr and Ejani Shakir; running back Dalton; tight end Preston Howard; offensive lineman Lockette; and quarterback Cardell Williams.

defensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's starting defense against UConn included Lavon Johnson, Eyan Thomas, Nahsir Taylor and Sidney Stewart in the front; Trey Reddick and Daniel Wingate at linebacker; and Jamare Glasker, Amari Jackson, Jordan Scruggs, Messiah Delhomme and Lavain Scruggs in the secondary.
Sidney Stewart recorded six tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble against UConn.
Derrick LeBlanc recorded two sacks against UConn, his first two sacks for Maryland.
Freshman Zion Elee recorded his first career sack and forced a fumble against UConn; DD Holmes recovered the fumble.
Maryland added defensive-line transfers Lavon Johnson, Derrick LeBlanc, Armon Parker and Jayvon Parker, along with defensive back Amari Jackson and linebackers Stephen Dean III and Jordan Williams.
Daniel Wingate, Maryland's 2025 leading tackler with 102 tackles, had started 26 consecutive games entering the Virginia Tech guide.

coaching_changes.fact: Clint Trickett became Maryland's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach during the 2026 offseason after serving as Jacksonville State's offensive coordinator in 2025.
Matt Barnes returned to Maryland as special teams coordinator, Randy Starks took over the defensive line and Kyle Schmitt took over the tight ends.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Maryland averaged 560.5 total yards, 315.5 passing yards, 245.0 rushing yards and 50.0 points per game.
Maryland converted 55.2 percent of its third downs through two games.
Maryland scored nine rushing touchdowns through its first two games.
Maryland had no turnovers in either of its first two games.
Against UConn, Maryland completed two second-quarter scoring drives of at least 90 yards, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.

defensive_context.fact: Through two games, Maryland allowed 154.0 total yards, 115.5 passing yards, 38.5 rushing yards and 7.0 points per game.
Maryland recorded 10 sacks through its first two games, led by DD Holmes with 2.5; Eyan Thomas and Derrick LeBlanc each had two.
Maryland held its first two opponents to a 26.9 percent third-down conversion rate.
Maryland had held 18 consecutive opponents below 300 passing yards through the UConn game.
Maryland's defense had not allowed a red-zone score through its first two games.

special_teams.fact: Kicker Sean O'Haire made all three of his field-goal attempts through two games, connecting from 26 and 36 yards against Hampton and 19 yards against UConn.
Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding averaged 17.0 yards on two punt returns through two games, including a 34-yard return.

other_relevant.fact: Maryland returned 71 percent of its 2025 production, including 68 percent on offense and 74 percent on defense.
Maryland's schedule lists the Nebraska game for Oct. 3, 2026, in Nebraska.
